question: RULE on DRC-4274, two asks. FIRST, approve the drafted rewrite of the issue body (additive — nothing was falsified, so nothing needed demoting), the narrow milestone correction, and the scope of the plan document itself: the six elements DEC-3 requires plus one the issue body did not cover — an intro-amendment section, because SECURITY.md Scope violation sentence enumerates FILE READS and this probe is SUBPROCESS EXECUTION, so without it E4 would promote a section into a Scope whose own violation clause does not reach it. The quota precedent handled exactly this the same way. SECOND, and this is the one that departs from a written rule: triage recommends review depth DOWN from full adversarial to two lenses plus an arbiter, and names the conflict openly rather than resolving it silently. Two rows of the AGENTS.md Calibrating Effort table both reach this change and disagree. Approving makes the groundwork document the next build, which is this workflow first repository change, first PR, first CI run and first merge.

artifacts.summary: Both checks the dispatch flagged are settled by exercise rather than by reading, and one of the dispatch own premises is refuted. docs/plans IS in the validator owned set — via a recursive glob at scripts/validate_plugins.py:1209, which is exactly why grepping for the word plans finds nothing — and it was proved by experiment on a git archive HEAD copy: pristine exit 0, a scratch plan file carrying one bad link and one bad anchor produced exactly two errors and exit 1. The CI change-detector was simulated by running the real is_prose function from quality-gate.yml against the live derived ASSERTED list: a new plan file classifies as prose, so this PR owes python3 scripts/validate_plugins.py and nothing else. The argument is structural rather than empirical — a file that does not yet exist cannot appear in a list derived from existing test literals. The dispatch claimed two tests open a docs/plans path literally; only one does. test_notifications.py:1300 carries the path in a comment, not an open, so the deny-list has one entry rather than two. The precedents were recovered from history rather than taken from description: the quota plan doc 84 lines and 4 headings, the ask-lane 193 lines and 9 headings, both deleted on promotion, giving a target of 110 plus or minus 30. Three further claims were re-derived rather than accepted: changed really is entries-not-files (2 entries for 4 changed files at git 2.55.0), the --no-spacedock respawn forwarding branch really exists at lifecycle.py:554-555, and nothing in the issue body was falsified, so the rewrite is purely additive. One gap the issue body did not cover was found and is the substantive addition to the deliverable: the Scope violation sentence enumerates file reads and this probe is subprocess execution, so the document needs an intro-amendment section naming the sentences that change, as the quota precedent had. Eight acceptance criteria, seven offline and one interactive — the interactive one declared as interactive with no harness planned rather than dressed up as a check — and a prose-grep AC over our own text is explicitly declared OUT with its reason and routed to review as a human instruction instead. No Linear write of any kind and no repository file touched: both experiments ran in throwaway directories under /tmp.
